reads.fact: In zone UH of Chevry, the building footprint must not exceed one third (1/3) of the total site area in the zone.
In zone UH of Chevry, buildings must be set back at least 4 metres from the current or planned alignment.
In zone UH of Chevry, the maximum height to the ridge (faîtage) is 10 metres in both sectors UHa and UHb.

In zone UH of Chevry, housing requires 2 parking spaces per dwelling in the general case, but 3 spaces per dwelling plus 1 visitor space per 3 dwellings in new housing developments (opérations d'ensemble nouvelles such as lotissements or permis groupés); both cases must be stated.
In zone UH of Chevry, the maximum height to the eaves is 3 metres in sector UHa and 5.50 metres in sector UHb.
In zone UH of Chevry, the maximum number of levels is R+Combles in sector UHa and R+1+Combles in sector UHb.
In zone UH of Chevry, buildings must be at least 2 metres from the side boundaries (limites séparatives) when there are no windows (vues).
In zone UH of Chevry, buildings must be at least 4 metres from the side boundaries when there are windows (vues) on the ground floor.
In zone UH of Chevry, windows (vues) on an upper floor may be opened only at least 6 metres from the side boundaries.

In zone UH of Chevry, article 7 on separative boundaries covers the lateral and the rear (fond de terrain) boundaries alike, so the rear setback is the same as the side setback (2 m without windows, 4 m with windows on the ground floor, 6 m for windows on upper floors).
In zone UH of Chevry, several buildings on one property must be at least 8 metres apart if at least one of the two facing facades has windows (vues).
In zone UH of Chevry, several buildings on one property must be at least 4 metres apart if neither facing facade has windows (vues).
In zone UH of Chevry, at least 50 percent of the parking spaces must be covered and integrated in the volume of the building at ground level.
In zone UH of Chevry, one high-stem tree must be planted per 150 m² of land free of construction, with a minimum of 2 trees per site.
In zone UH of Chevry, housing is admitted under the condition that it fits the architectural and landscape harmony of the place.

facts.key_or_statement: The OAP chapter 8 (quartier Joliot Curie) applies to the site and its orientations come in addition to those of chapter 7 (site de Moulon), so chapters 7 and 8 apply together.
For buildings with housing as main destination, the OAP asks for varied building heights (épannelage) reaching an average objective of R+4; this is an objective, not a maximum height.
Along rue Joliot-Curie, buildings should be set on the alignment of the street, without creating a uniform continuous built front (porosity and views towards block interiors are sought).

The programming of the Joliot-Curie district includes housing for students, researchers and families, next to higher education and research, public facilities, shops, services and economic activities.
Family and student housing programmes are located mainly in the west of the district, close to services and public facilities.
Chapter 7 states that in UM zones the heights and gabarits are set by the règlement, with the exception of the Joliot Curie district classed UMG.
To limit car use, the OAP asks for underground car parks or car parks within the building volume, pooled parking, and few spaces along the streets.
The OAP describes rue Joliot-Curie as the structuring east-west axis with a gabarit of about 20 m, shared between cars, cyclists and pedestrians.
Ground floors housing common spaces, shops or facilities must open onto the public space, with an adapted height.
The landscape orientation is a landscape framework resting on the wooded slope (coteau boisé) and supporting an alternative management of rainwater.

citation.quote: Cette zone fait l’objet d’orientations d’aménagement, document n°3 du PLU (orientations 8 et 9) avec lesquelles tout projet d’aménagement et de construction doit être compatible.
Le projet d’aménagement de Moulon comprend le quartier Joliot Curie pour lequel des orientations d’aménagement spécifiques sont définies.
Les orientations générales pour le projet d’aménagement de Moulon sont les suivantes :
Créer un quartier aux usages mixtes, susceptible de favoriser les rencontres et constituer des lieux de vie attractifs et animés, réunissant l’ensemble des composantes urbaines ;
Pour les constructions à destination principale d’habitation, un épannelage des constructions devra permettre d’atteindre un objectif de R+4 moyen.
Le principe d’une implantation des constructions à l’alignement le long de la voie doit être retenu.

citation.article: ARTICLE 9 - zone UMG -EMPRISE AU SOL DES CONSTRUCTIONS
citation.quote: L’emprise au sol des constructions n’est pas réglementée, toutefois, tout projet doit être compatible avec les orientations d’aménagement et de programmation définies au document 3 du PLU.

la limitation de l’utilisation de la voiture, avec la réalisation de parkings souterrains ou dans le gabarit des constructions, avec une recherche de mutualisation des places de stationnement et l’accueil d’un nombre réduit de places de stationnement le long des voies,
en dimensionnant l’offre intégrée pour chaque construction ;
L’accessibilité vers les stations implantées au nord du quartier Joliot-Curie doit être privilégiée dans le choix de tracé des emprises publiques.
Installer une trame paysagère sur le site, qui s’appuie sur les qualités de son environnement, et notamment sur le coteau boisé, et qui soit le support d’une gestion alternative de l’eau pluviale.
Un axe structurant Nord-Sud, dispositif paysager qui s’étend des coteaux boisés au Sud et se prolonge au Nord au-delà du quartier Joliot-Curie.
Le cœur du quartier reçoit un traitement paysager en cohérence avec le grand paysage et l’aménagement de la lisière.
constructions d'habitation destinées aux étudiants, aux chercheurs et aux familles
les programmes de logements familiaux et étudiants sont implantés principalement à l’Ouest du quartier pour favoriser la mixité
A l’ouest du quartier Joliot-Curie se constitue un lieu, propice à l’implantation de programmes de logements familiaux et d’étudiants accompagnés de commerces et d’équipements.
La variété des constructions destinées aux logements doit permettre d’offrir des logements accessibles à tous et un mode d’habitat différencié.
Afin de limiter les émissions de gaz à effet de serre sur le site, le projet prévoit :

The landscape orientation is a landscape framework resting on the wooded slope (coteau boisé) and supporting an alternative management of rainwater.

Housing in zone UM requires bicycle parking only for buildings of more than three dwellings, at 0.75 m² per dwelling up to two main rooms and 1.5 m² per dwelling otherwise.

la hauteur de la construction mesurée à l’égout du toit (L=H) avec un minimum de 8 mètres dés lors que la façade concernée comporte de vues ;

Les constructions doivent être implantées en retrait des limites séparatives latérales et de fond de terrain.

facts.key_or_statement: In UHe, the footprint of main buildings must not exceed 20 percent of the site area (article UH9 rule "En UH et UHe et UHf").
In UHe, the footprint of ancillary buildings must not exceed 5 percent of the site area, and terraces and swimming pools count as footprint.
UHe has no height rule of its own; the general UH rule (UH outside UHf) applies, so a main building is limited to 7 metres at the eaves or the acroterion.

Setback from side and rear boundaries must be at least 8 metres where the facade has views, and half the facade height (H/2) with a minimum of 2 metres where it has none.
Several buildings on one plot must be at least 8 metres apart if at least one of the facing facades has views, and 4 metres apart if neither has views.
In UH, UHe and UHf, vegetated spaces must cover at least 70 percent of the site area.

What sets UHe apart is the residual radioactive contamination of its districts (Coudraies, Clos Rose); the regulation only allows dwellings or extensions of existing buildings there, under conditions.
In UHe, any exploitation of subsoil natural resources (quarry, water abstraction, hydrocarbons) is additionally forbidden.

In the prescription perimeter, housing construction and works, with their outbuildings and garages, are authorised provided that any work requiring excavation is accompanied by removal of the soil by an approved body to a specialised treatment or storage centre.

In the prescription perimeter, excavation deeper than 50 cm over a surface of 10 m² or more requires prior information of the municipal services and a prior radiological mapping (dose rate) of the area.
In the prescription perimeter, a check of the bottom of the excavation must be done before the foundations are laid.

facts.key_or_statement: In zone N (Vallée), article N1 prohibits, throughout the zone and its sectors, new constructions, works or structures for housing (habitation), other than those admitted by article N2.

In zone N (Vallée), article N2 does not admit any new dwelling in the plain zone; the only housing-related use it admits for the whole zone is the extension of dwellings existing at the approval date of the PLU, limited to 15 percent of their floor area (surface de plancher).

The 20 percent extension limit for existing constructions applies only in the sector Nc, not in the plain zone N.
Housing-related development linked to existing activities (aménagement d’habitat) is admitted only in the sector Nca, and only for activities authorised in existing buildings.
The footprint limit of 15 percent in article N9 applies only in the sectors Nc, Nca and NL; for the other sectors, including plain zone N, it is "sans objet".
Under article N10, the height of constructions in plain zone N is not regulated; the 10 metre ridge limit applies only in the sectors Nc, Nca and NL.
Under article N6, constructions must be set back at least 12 metres from the axis of the road or from the limits of public land (emprise publique).
Under article N7, the setback from property boundaries (limites séparatives) must be at least 16 metres, and 8 metres only in Nca.
Under article N8, the distance between several buildings on one property is not regulated in zone N and the sector NL; the 8 metre minimum applies only in the sectors Nc and Nca.
The regulation's Titre III lists an emplacement réservé Z at the Impasse de la Gourdillerie, a turning area (aire de retournement) of 490 m² for the commune.
Under Titre III, construction is prohibited on land, built or not, included in an emplacement réservé, subject to the Code de l’urbanisme.

must_flag.question: must_flag
must_flag.subject: UMG article 12 sets no fixed parking ratio for a public service or collective-interest building (the number of spaces depends on the facility's nature, grouping, public-transport access and nearby public car parks; only higher education and research has 1 space per 170 m2), so the study must flag that the parking requirement cannot be fixed without knowing the facility.
must_flag.reason: Ambiguity 11 asks "What number of parking spaces applies to the building under Article 12.1?", records the choice "number determined by needs (no fixed ratio)", and notes that floor area is unknown so no figure can be computed and the number must be justified at permit stage. Ambiguities 3 and 23 raise the same point.

must_flag.question: must_flag
must_flag.subject: The 25 m PLU height limit and the article 9 absence of a footprint limit are both subject to compatibility with the OAP (document 3), whose only quantified height objective (R+4 on average) concerns housing; the OAP gives no height or footprint figure for a facility.
must_flag.reason: Ambiguity 15 asks whether the OAP's R+4 average height objective applies to a facility or only to housing, and records the choice 'Only to housing; the R+4 objective does not bind the facility', so the 25 m limit governs. This covers the expected point about the quantified OAP height objective applying only to housing.

must_not.question: must_not

must_not.reason: The output sets the facility's maximum height at 25 m (UMG 10.2) and says a mixed building "falls to 18 m". It mentions 18 m and 20 m only as the alternative if the 25 m rule is rejected, never as the height of the facility, and 20 m is never tied to this facility's height as the claim requires.

must_not.question: must_not

must_not.question: must_not

anti_patterns.reason: The study sends the reader elsewhere on the ABF and noise rules: "Architecte des Bâtiments de France and noise-zone rules must be checked on the annex plans, which were not read." anti_patterns.question: invented_rule
anti_patterns.reason: The networks condition cites [14, 15, 16] for "release limited to 0.7 L/s/ha", and none of those quotes contains that figure. Similarly, the bicycle figures (0.75 m², 1.5 m², 3 m²) cite [28], whose quote only says "plus de trois logements :", with no ellipsis marking a cut.

anti_patterns.question: restating
anti_patterns.reason: Several conditions are copied with no resolved value or verdict for this site. Examples are "one tree per 300 m² of plot" (no tree count), "release limited to 0.7 L/s/ha" (no flow figure for the 3,431 m² plot), and the appearance and access rules, which are quoted without saying how they bear on the building.

anti_patterns.question: inconsistency
anti_patterns.reason: The summary and narrative match the typed fields: zone UM5a, a 2,745 m² footprint, 20 m height, 54,900 m³ volume with fits = true, 686 m² green space, the 6 m / 3 m / 1 m setbacks, and the 1 per 35 m² parking norm with 85% built into the building. The legend items, the 'permitted' verdict and the parcel area (3,431 geometric vs 3,429 cadastral) also agree throughout.

anti_patterns.question: unflagged_gap
anti_patterns.reason: The external references are either flagged as unread or only repeated without content. ABF and noise rules are marked "annex plans, which were not read", and the Code de l'urbanisme categories are recorded as "not in the corpus". The energy line ("at least the norms in force") restates the reference and applies no content from it as settled.

anti_patterns.question: hedging
anti_patterns.reason: Each limit is either a single value or a value with its condition, such as "8 m with views; max(2 m, H/2) without views". Every open point is settled with a recorded choice, for example "Façade with views assumed: 8 m" and "Vallée UA chapter". The 35-45° roof pitch is the regulation's own stated range, not an undecided value.

anti_patterns.question: deferral
anti_patterns.reason: The study sends the reader elsewhere on points it should settle from the cited documents: "Until the commune or the cadastre confirms that the parcels are outside ER 12", "Obtain the cadastre-to-plan confirmation of ER 12 from the commune", and "Noise-insulation and archaeological checks are not done". These are deferrals, not just recorded ambiguities.

anti_patterns.question: invented_rule
anti_patterns.reason: The parking row states "Spaces at least 2.50 m x 5 m" and cycle areas of "0.75 m² per dwelling... 1.5 m² otherwise", citing [6-9]. None of those quotes contains these figures, and the quotes are not cut off with an ellipsis. The appearance line also gives "Pitched roofs 35-45°" and fence heights of 1.80 m and 2 m, citing [15, 16], which hold only the ABF consultation and "toitures terrasses peuvent être admises".

anti_patterns.question: restating
anti_patterns.reason: The without-views setback is left as a formula, "max(2 m, 0.5 x H)", with no figure, though H is known to be 9 m. The Other conditions also quote pitched roofs "35-45°", fence heights and "Noise-insulation band" rules without saying how they bear on this building.

anti_patterns.question: inconsistency
anti_patterns.reason: The narrative figures match the typed fields: 243.6 m² cap, 151.6 m² and 1,364.4 m³ proposal, 2,192.6 m³ maximum, 2 spaces per dwelling, a conditional verdict and no legend item applying. The one loose point is ambiguity 19 saying the list names "CA5 and CA6", but that is a narrative slip, not a contradiction of a typed field.

anti_patterns.question: unflagged_gap
anti_patterns.reason: Each externally referenced rule is flagged as unread: noise bands ("annex plan (pièce 8), which was not read"), archaeological rules and flood sectors ("not checked"), and the Code de l'urbanisme exception on reserves ("unless the Code de l'urbanisme provides otherwise"). open_points.question: What is the width (emprise) of Chemin de Moulon, so as to know whether UH6.3 (a) 9 m from the road centre-line applies, and what distance results from the road limit?
options: Use 9 m from the road limit (more restrictive reading, adopted for this study as the project lead's decision)
Road emprise of 8 m or more: 5 m from the alignment under UH6.3 (b)
Road emprise below 8 m: 9 m from the road centre-line, so about 9 m minus half the emprise from the limit
open_points.why: The site artifact gives the public-land edge length (46.3 m) but not the road width, and the notes do not give the emprise. The 9 m from the road limit is a conservative reading adopted by the project lead, not a value read from the documents.

options: House kept outside the EBC as drawn on the plan
EBC geometry needed from the graphic regulation or cadastre
open_points.why: The site artifact has no EBC polygon; the EBC is only described as the western part of the parcel in the legend. The envelope was not clipped to the EBC, so compliance with UH9.3 and UH13.1 must be checked on the surveyed EBC outline.

open_points.question: Does the 8 m setback from an EBC limit with the public emprise (UH6.3, sentence placed under 'Dans le secteur UHf') apply in the generic UH zone to the parcel's western EBC part, which does not front the road?
options: Yes: applies in all of zone UH
No: applies only in sector UHf
open_points.why: The notes flag that the scope of this sentence is not explicit. The study assumes the road-side setback of 9 m only; the EBC-limit 8 m rule is not applied because the EBC does not touch the public emprise on the plan.

open_points.question: Is the 7 m maximum height to the égout du toit (eaves) for a main building in Vallée - UH to be applied as a separate envelope limit, since the envelope takes a single maximum height of 10 m to the ridge?
options: Use 10 m to the ridge only (as submitted), with 7 m to eaves to be checked at design stage
Cap the volume at 7 m eaves with a 10 m ridge (a pitched roof envelope)
open_points.why: The envelope tool accepts one maximum height per building; the notes give 7 m to eaves and 10 m to ridge (UH10.2). The volume returned (7,635.8 m³) assumes a 10 m height over the whole footprint, which overstates the volume if eaves are at 7 m.

open_points.question: Which UH zone applies to the parcel: Vallée - UH or Chevry - UH?
options: Vallée - UH (taken by the project lead for this study)
Chevry - UH

open_points.question: Whether the façade height H used for the H/2 retrait is measured to the égout du toit (7 m) as the notes state, which gives a 3.5 m setback without vues, given that the setback is applied here only with vues (8 m).
options: H to the égout du toit (about 7 m), giving H/2 = 3.5 m without vues

open_points.why: UH7.2.2 defines H as the façade height to the égout du toit, but the envelope tool applies the ratio to the building height it is given. With vues assumed on all façades the 8 m distance governs, so the choice does not change the proposal; it matters only if the façades are blind.

must_flag.subject: About 39 percent of the parcel (1475 m2) is covered by an Espace Boisé Classé, which UH13.1 protects from any occupation compromising the woodland; the buildable ground is reduced and this partial overlay must be raised.
must_flag.reason: Ambiguities 18 and 23 are recorded as open points on the EBC: 18 asks "Where exactly is the Espace Boisé Classé on parcel 91272000CO0051 (the western strip), and does the house footprint stay outside it?" and 23 asks whether the EBC pattern falls inside the site, choosing "EBC covers the western part of the outline; the house is kept outside it". Both raise the partial EBC overlay and its limit on buildable ground, even though neither gives the 39 % / 1475 m² figure.

must_flag.question: must_flag
must_flag.subject: UH article 6 sets the road setback at 5 m from the alignment when the road right-of-way is 8 m or more, or 9 m from the road axis when it is under 8 m, and eases it along chemins and sentes (6.4); the right-of-way width of the Chemin de Moulon is not in the corpus and the applicable alternative must be established or raised.
must_flag.reason: Ambiguity 17 asks "What is the width (emprise) of Chemin de Moulon, so as to know whether UH6.3 (a) 9 m from the road centre-line applies", sets out both the 5 m and 9 m alternatives, and records the choice of the 9 m reading because the road width is not in the site data.

must_flag.question: must_flag
must_flag.subject: UH article 7 restricts main buildings to a 25 m constructibility band measured from the roads serving the plot, beyond which only terraces and annexes are allowed; the study must raise how this band limits the usable ground.
must_flag.reason: Ambiguity 7 asks what setback rule applies within the 25 m band measured from access routes, and its options include "Outside the band: only annexes and terraces may be built, not the main house". It records the choice made (house within the band, position not measured). Caveat 4 also lists the 25 m band as unmeasured.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: States a minimum plot size (superficie minimale des terrains constructibles) as a rule applying in UH.
must_not.reason: The output lists setbacks, footprint (20%), green area, height and parking rules for UH, but never states a minimum plot size (superficie minimale des terrains constructibles). The only nearby mention is access as a condition for buildability (UH3.2), which is not a plot-size rule.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: States a COS (coefficient d'occupation du sol) or a floor-area ratio as a rule applying in UH.
must_not.reason: The output states a footprint ratio rule for UH: "Maximum footprint ratio | 20%: UH9.2: footprint of main buildings at most 20% of the plot area." This is a ground-coverage ratio (emprise au sol), not a COS or a floor-area ratio, so it does not match the claim.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: States that the footprint limit is one third of the site area, that the road setback is 4 m, or that heights or levels follow UHa or UHb (Chevry UH values), or cites the Chevry - UH chapter (regulation PDF pages 256 to 268) as the source of the rules.
must_not.reason: The output applies the Vallée - UH chapter (20% footprint, 9 m or 5 m road setback, 10 m height) and cites Chevry UH only as the unchosen option, for the architectural-harmony condition on housing (p.257). It never states a one-third footprint, a 4 m road setback, UHa/UHb heights, or Chevry UH as the source of its rules.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: Applies the values of sector UHc, UHd, UHe or UHf (for example 25 or 30 percent footprint, 11 m height, 15 m road setback) to the site.
must_not.reason: The output applies generic UH values (20% footprint, 10 m height, 9 m road setback) and, in ambiguities 2 and 4, rejects the UHc/UHd/UHe/UHf sub-sectors: "No letter: generic UH of the Vallée chapter". It mentions UHf values only as a rejected option.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: Treats the site as free of the Espaces Boisés Classés, or places the proposed building or its footprint on the EBC part of the parcel.
must_not.reason: The output states the western part of the parcel is an EBC and that the house "must stay outside it" and is "kept away from the western strip, which is the EBC". It neither treats the site as EBC-free nor places the building on the EBC.

must_not.question: must_not

must_not.reason: The output rejects both: the legend table says PPRi 'lies about 130 m south' and 'Zone humide | No wetland pattern on the outline'; ambiguity 4 chooses 'no ... PPRI perimeter on the parcel'. Neither applies to the site.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: Uses a parcel other than CO0051 (for example the neighbouring CO0050, CO0052 or CO0054) as the study site.
must_not.reason: The output uses CO0051 as the study site throughout. It names CO0050, CO0052, CO0053, CO0054 and CO0048 only to set them aside: "Set aside: 91272000CO0052 ... 91272000CO0050 ... too narrow and small to be the site on its own".

anti_patterns.question: hedging
anti_patterns.reason: Each point with alternatives is settled by a recorded choice (road setback "Use 9 m from the road limit", Vallée over Chevry), and the other multi-value items such as "H/2 with a 2 m minimum" or 35-45° roof pitches are formulas or the regulation's own range, so nothing is left uncommitted.

anti_patterns.question: deferral
anti_patterns.reason: Several points are sent elsewhere instead of being answered from the documents, e.g. ambiguity 6: "any felling is to be checked with the authority" and "Not decided"; the EBC outline is also left "to be checked on the surveyed EBC outline", and the chapter choice is "flagged for confirmation".

anti_patterns.question: invented_rule
anti_patterns.reason: The height condition says "at most 7 m to the égout du toit" and cites [19, 20, 25]. Those quotes only give 10 m to the faîtage, R+1+combles and the opening words "ne doit pas excéder :", so the 7 m eaves figure appears in none of them.

anti_patterns.question: restating
anti_patterns.reason: The conditions list restates "one high-stem tree per 100 m² of plot" with no resolved count for this 3,817.9 m² plot. It also quotes access, network, roof-pitch (35-45°) and fence (1.80 m) rules without saying how they bear on the house or whether the site meets them.

anti_patterns.question: inconsistency
anti_patterns.reason: The summary's figures match the typed fields: 20% footprint (763.6 m²), 10 m height, 7,635.8 m³ volume (the windows/proposal envelope), 70% green (2,672.5 m²), the 9 m and 8 m setbacks, the 2-space parking rule, the UH zone and the 'permitted' verdict. The narrative sections also agree with them. The parcel's recorded 3,821 m² against the 3,817.9 m² computed site area is explained as a recorded versus computed figure, not a contradiction.

anti_patterns.question: unflagged_gap
anti_patterns.reason: Rules that point outside the PLU, such as the EBC rule citing L.130-1 of the code de l'urbanisme, are caveated: the study says the felling procedure 'needs the procedure to be settled (open point)'. The other cross-references (lexicon norms, definitions) point to pages the study actually read.

must_flag.question: must_flag
must_flag.subject: AURc article 2 authorises an operation only if its site covers at least 9000 m2, waived for residual plots not integrated in a partial development; the parcel (about 3400 m2, part of a zone of about 34000 m2) is below the threshold and the documents do not settle whether it counts as a residual plot or whether the operation compromises the coherent development of the zone.
must_flag.reason: Ambiguity 1 asks whether AURc2's 9000 m² minimum blocks the 3,406 m² parcel and whether the 'terrains résiduels non intégrés à l'aménagement partiel' exception applies. Its chosen answer records that the exception is 'not established'. The question about the zone's coherent development is not raised, but the residual-plot question is.

must_flag.question: must_flag
must_flag.subject: UR article 10 (referred to by AURc10) gives two heights, 7 m at the eaves or acrotere and 10 m at the ridge; the single height used for the envelope depends on the roof form and must be stated as a choice or open point.
must_flag.reason: Ambiguity 12 records the height band choice: "height band 7 m at eaves/acrotère and 10 m at ridge. The envelope uses 7 m." This is a recorded choice on which of the two heights to use for the envelope, even though it is framed as a parking/height band question.

must_flag.question: must_flag
must_flag.subject: The AURc6 road setback is 5 m when the road right-of-way is 8 m or more and 6 m otherwise; the right-of-way width of Route de Damiette is not in the corpus.
must_flag.reason: Ambiguities 2 and 28 ask which road setback applies on Route de Damiette, 5 m (emprise 8 m or more) or 6 m, note that the emprise "is not in the documents or the site data", and record the choice of 6 m.

must_flag.question: must_flag
must_flag.subject: The Damiette OAP (chapter 4) gives qualitative orientations (about 15 dwellings, view corridor, green strip to be kept unbuilt, access from Route de Damiette) on a perimeter far larger than the parcel; how they bind this parcel and a single collective building needs a justified reading.
must_flag.reason: Ambiguity 16 asks how the 'environ 15 logements' figure applies to a single collective building on a ~3,406 m² parcel and records the choice ('Indicative capacity for the whole sector; it does not cap or set a minimum'). Ambiguities 17, 25 and 26 also record how the green strip, view perspective and access apply to this parcel.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: States that AURc has no height rule, or that no height limit applies to the building, or gives a height figure without saying that article AURc10 refers to the rules of zone UR.
must_not.reason: The output gives height figures (7 m eaves, 10 m ridge) and says they come from "UR10 via AURc10", citing AURc10: "Les règles applicables sont celles de la zone UR." It never says AURc has no height rule or that no limit applies.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: States that the maximum height of a main building in AURc is 10 metres at the eaves or acrotere, or 7 metres at the ridge.
must_not.reason: The output gives the opposite of the claim: "at most 7 m to the eaves or acrotère and 10 m to the ridge, faîte or ceiling height". It never states 10 m at the eaves/acrotère or 7 m at the ridge.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: States that the AURc footprint limit is 10 percent (UR) or 13 percent (URa), or that AURc defers to UR for footprint.
must_not.reason: The output states the AURc footprint limit as 20 % (AURc9.2, "at most 20 % of the total area of the terrain"). It never gives 10 % or 13 % for footprint and never says AURc defers to UR for footprint; the only 10 % mentioned is common green space.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: Applies the UR road setback (10 m from the alignment, 14 m from the axis) to AURc, or states that AURc defers to UR for the road setback.
must_not.reason: The output applies AURc6 to the road setback: 5 m if the road emprise is 8 m or more, 6 m otherwise, with 6 m retained. It never applies a UR road setback of 10 m from the alignment or 14 m from the axis to AURc, and it does not say AURc defers to UR for the road setback.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: States that AURc imposes no numeric minimum for planted or green space, or applies a 20 percent green figure from another zone.
must_not.reason: The output states that AURc13.2 requires at least 75 % of the terrain in vegetated spaces ("Au minimum 75% ... espaces végétalisés"), so it does impose a numeric minimum and does not apply a 20 % green figure; the 20 % figure is used only for footprint (AURc9.2). The Moulon wording from other zones is explicitly not used.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: States that no OAP applies to the site, or relies on another OAP chapter (for example chapter 5 Rougemonts) instead of chapter 4 Damiette (AURc).
must_not.reason: The output states "OAP applicable: **yes**" and relies on the Damiette OAP (section 4, AURc1/AURc2). It never says no OAP applies, and never substitutes another chapter such as Rougemonts.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: States without qualification that the operation meets the AURc2 minimum site area of 9000 m2.
must_not.reason: The output says the parcel is 3,406 m², below the 9,000 m² minimum, and calls admissibility 'conditional, not confirmed'. It never asserts that the operation meets the minimum site area.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: Uses a parcel other than BD0231 (for example the neighbouring BD0021, BD0225 or BD0263) as the study site.
must_not.reason: The output uses BD0231 as the study site throughout ("The site is the single cadastral parcel BD0231"). BD0225, BD0263 and BD0021 are only named in the "Set aside" list, which rejects them as study sites.

anti_patterns.question: hedging
anti_patterns.reason: Every multi-value item is either a condition-based rule (e.g. "8 m where the façade has vues, 4 m ... in the contrary case"; 7 m eaves vs 10 m ridge) or an ambiguity settled by a choice (road setback: "6 m (the stricter value)"). The study commits to one value each time, so it does not hedge.

anti_patterns.question: deferral
anti_patterns.reason: The study sends the reader elsewhere for points it should answer itself, e.g. the 9,000 m² blocking point "must be settled with the planning authority before design commitments", and "the secured layout is to be agreed with the authority". The PPRi check is also "to be confirmed against the PPRi document itself".

anti_patterns.question: invented_rule
anti_patterns.reason: Several figures are in none of the quotes cited for them. The access widths "3.50 m one-way, 4 m ... 6 m" cite [9,10], but quote 10 stops at "largeur minimum de :" with no figures. The "2 m on separative limits" fence height cites [27-29], and only 1.80 m appears there. The "12 m if one does" spacing is absent from quotes [20,21].

anti_patterns.question: restating
anti_patterns.reason: The 'appearance' condition restates roof pitches "between 35 and 45 degrees" and fences "1.80 m maximum on the road, 2 m on separative limits" without saying how they bear on this building. The access widths ("3.50 m one-way, 4 m for fewer than 30 parking spaces") are likewise left unresolved for the site.

anti_patterns.question: inconsistency
anti_patterns.reason: The narrative matches the typed fields: conditional verdict, 681.2 m² footprint, 4,768 m³ and 6,812 m³ volumes, 1,326 m² usable area, about 2,555 m² green, and 2 spaces per dwelling with one covered. The 3,406 m² against 3,413 m² gap is explained in the text as the computed area against the cadastral figure.

anti_patterns.question: unflagged_gap
anti_patterns.reason: Each external reference is flagged as unread. The Code de l'urbanisme list is "not in the corpus", and the PPRi absence is marked "To be confirmed against the PPRi document itself". The OAP was read, and the UR rules cited via AURc are in the regulation.

layout.reasons: Indicative reference only. One detached house on the whole parcel, the envelope being the area left after the setbacks: 16 m from all limits (the code labels every edge side/rear, since the site has no identified road frontage; 16 m is the stricter of the two distances, so the result holds for the 12 m road setback too). Height at the 10 m Nc ridge cap as a conservative reference. The building is NOT permitted by N1 in zone N: this envelope shows only what the setbacks would allow.

bounds.name: largest
assumptions: Each limit at its smallest allowed distance, 0 where building on it is allowed: the legal maximum.

bounds.name: windows
assumptions: Every facade facing a limit has windows: each limit at its distance with windows (else without, else 0 where building on it is allowed).

proposal.name: proposal
assumptions: Every facade facing a limit has windows: each limit at its distance with windows (else without, else 0 where building on it is allowed).

open_points.question: Is a new detached house on parcel 91272000CC0152 permitted at all? N1 prohibits new housing in zone N and its sectors, and N2 admits only extensions of existing houses (15% of surface de plancher; 20% in Nc).
options: Not permitted: no article admits a new house on a free plot (verdict retained)
Permitted only as an extension of a house existing at PLU approval (the parcel's existing house, if any, is not in the context)
open_points.why: The written regulation contains no express exception for a new dwelling in N or Nc; the envelope here is indicative only.

open_points.question: In which sector does the parcel lie: zone N proper, or the Nc sub-sector (north-west part, per the legend)? The Nc boundary is not measured.
options: Whole parcel in zone N: no height limit, no footprint limit (N9 sans objet)
Nc part: 10 m at the ridge and 15% footprint, which would cap this envelope at about 904 m² of footprint (15% of 6,028.6 m²)
Mixed: 15% and 10 m on the Nc part only
open_points.why: The règlement graphique is image-only; the envelope assumes the whole parcel is in zone N, as instructed, and the Nc alternative is noted.

open_points.question: Which edge of the parcel is the road frontage for the 12 m setback under N6? The site has no identified road edge: the code labels all eight edges as side/rear (16 m), and the access strip CC0193 is not public land.
options: 12 m from the axe de la voie on the impasse frontage (if a public road is confirmed there)
16 m on all limits (as computed)
open_points.why: The site artifact shows no public-land edge; the 12 m road distance is therefore not applied to any edge, and 16 m is more restrictive on every limit.

open_points.question: Is there a graphic non aedificandi indication or a forest-edge (lisière) on the parcel that would exclude construction areas under N9, and where does the zone humide (western part) lie?
options: Yes: construction forbidden on the delimited part, which would reduce the envelope
No indication on the parcel: the envelope is unchanged
open_points.why: The zoning plan was only seen at overview scale; the zone humide prohibition (Titre I 3.5) has no numeric buffer in the notes.

open_points.question: Height: N10 is non réglementé in zone N but 10 m au faîtage in Nc. Since a numeric height is required, the 10 m Nc cap was used as the reference. Confirm the height basis for the reference.
options: 10 m au faîtage (Nc cap, retained)
No limit in zone N (height would be set by other rules only)
open_points.why: The contract requires a positive height; the notes give no limit for zone N.

must_flag.question: must_flag
must_flag.subject: The emplacement réservé covers only part of the parcel (about 58%), not the whole parcel.
must_flag.reason: No ambiguity asks whether a reserved site (emplacement réservé) covers part of the parcel. The legend table says the reserved-site symbols are "not present on the outline", which is not a recorded open point, and the partial coverage (about 58%) is never raised.

must_flag.question: must_flag
must_flag.subject: The only housing item admitted in zone N is the extension of dwellings existing at the PLU approval date (15% of floor area); the program states no existing dwelling on the parcel, so it must not be assumed.
must_flag.reason: Ambiguity 10 asks whether the N2 extension clause 'L’extension des habitations existantes à la date d’approbation du présent PLU' covers a new house on a parcel without an existing house, and records the choice 'No'. Ambiguities 1 and 19 also record that only extension of an existing dwelling is admitted and that the context does not mention one.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: States or implies that the new house is permitted, conditional or restricted in zone N, or delivers a buildable envelope, height or footprint for it as if it were allowed.
must_not.reason: The output states the house is "PROHIBITED" in zone N (N1/N2). The envelope of 1,988 m² and 10 m is labelled "indicative only… since the building is not permitted" and "not an authorisation", so it does not treat the house as allowed.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: Treats the N2 extension of existing dwellings as permission to build a new dwelling.
must_not.reason: The output rejects the claim: it says N2 admits only extensions of existing houses and that a new detached house is prohibited ("No article admits a new detached house"; ambiguity 10 answers "No: the clause only covers extensions"). It never treats the extension clause as permission for a new dwelling.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: Applies the figures of the sectors Nc, Nca or NL to plain zone N (20% extension, 15% footprint, 10 m ridge height, 8 m spacing between buildings).
must_not.reason: The envelope takes the 10 m Nc ridge height for a parcel treated as plain zone N ("height reference 10 m (Nc cap)"), and ambiguity 23 retains it. The output does say N10 is unregulated in N proper and labels the figure an indicative reference, but it still applies an Nc figure to zone N.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: Uses the zone N rules of the Chevry chapter instead of the Vallée chapter.
must_not.reason: The output applies the Vallée N chapter and chooses "Zone N (Vallée) sector N" (ambiguity 8). Chevry N is listed only as a rejected option, so the claim is not asserted.

must_not.question: must_not
must_not.subject: Uses a neighbouring parcel (CC0199, CC0198, CC0152 or CC0201) as the study site instead of CC0193.
must_not.reason: The output states "Site = parcel 91272000CC0152 alone" and sets aside CC0193 as an access strip, so the study site is the neighbouring parcel CC0152 instead of CC0193.

anti_patterns.question: hedging
anti_patterns.reason: The study commits to one value for each limit: 16 m on all limits, 10 m height, and no footprint limit in N. The Nc alternative ("If the Nc part applied, the 15% footprint cap would be about 904 m²") is conditional and is settled by a chosen option in the recorded ambiguities.

anti_patterns.question: deferral
anti_patterns.reason: Several points are passed back to the reader instead of being answered, e.g. the PPRi is "judged not to apply, to be confirmed at cadastral scale", the wetland perimeter "must be checked", and "Confirm the height basis for the reference". These are the same kind of deferral as "to be confirmed by the instructing service".

anti_patterns.question: invented_rule
anti_patterns.reason: Ambiguity 1 gives the N2 extension cap as "15%, or 20% in Nc", and the 20% figure appears in none of the quotes (quote 3 only says 15%). The access condition that accesses "must meet safety and fire-defence requirements" is likewise absent from quote 4.

anti_patterns.question: restating
anti_patterns.reason: Several conditions are only restated. The networks item says to connect to the sewer "where it exists" and never says whether a sewer exists at the site. The ABF opinion, N11 landscape integration and N13 tree-felling rules are copied as generic text with no statement of how they bear on this house.

anti_patterns.question: inconsistency
anti_patterns.reason: The narrative figures match the typed fields: footprint of about 1,988 m² and volume of about 19,878 m³ against 1987.8 m² and 19877.9 m³, the 904 m² Nc cap against 15% of 6,028.6 m², and a prohibited verdict throughout. The 16 m and 12 m setbacks, the Zone humide as the only applying legend item, and 'No number of spaces' against 'No parking requirement recorded' also agree.

anti_patterns.question: unflagged_gap
anti_patterns.reason: The study draws all its rules from the PLU articles it cites (N1, N2, N6, N7, Titre I). It also flags what it did not read, e.g. "Any other route would need a document not read here" and "Permitted through some other document ... not read here". It never states content from an outside code or appendix as settled.
